steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat peanut butter, brown sugar, white sugar, shortening, and margarine in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until smooth and creamy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until well blended.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; stir into creamed mixture until incorporated. Mix in oats until just combined.
Drop teaspoonfuls of dough onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake cookies in the preheated oven until just lightly browned, 10 to 15 minutes. Do not overbake. Cool and store in an airtight container.

review.reviewBody: These are fantastic! I've made them several times, and I find that I like them with extra oats (1/2 cup or so), less sugar, and with unsalted butter (I don't use shortening or margarine because they're scary). I often add chocolate chips to some of them, as well. For those who get flat cookies, there are three likely problems: a) your fat is too warm. Your shortening/marg/butter should be almost chilled--just barely warm enough to be creamed with the sugar. Anything warmer, and you're likely to spread. Also, don't cream them so long that the fat warms up; b) warm baking sheets. If you put dough onto a cookie sheet still warm from the last batch, you're asking for it. It's best if both the dough and the pan are cool; c) if neither of the above seems to be the problem, try adding another 1/4 cup of flour (or just make sure you were adding the proper amount in the first place). Hope this helps.

HAD TO TRY AFTER READING REVIEWS AND MADE MODIFICATIONS...MY FAMILY RAVED ABOUT THESE...BEST I EVER MADE, HAD TO RATION THEM OUT...MY MODIFICATIONS WERE; ADD 1TSP VANILLA, INCREASE FLOUR TO 1 3/4 CUP FLOUR...INCREASE OATMEAL TO 1 1/2 CUPS....USE 1 CUP CRUNCHY PEANUT BUTTER PLUS 1/2 CUP CREAMY PEATNUT BUTTER...DECREASE SALT TO 1/2 TSP.. I ALSO USED `1/2 CUP BUTTER AND 1/2 CUP CRISCO BUTTER FLAVOR SHORTENING....ADDED 1 PKG.SEMI-SWEET CHOCOLATE CHIPS..... BAKE ONLY 10 MINUTES...WE ALL HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS VERSION

ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! I subsituted 1 cup of butter instead of the margarine and shortening and it made the PERFECT cookie. THANK YOU THANK YOU.. deeeelicious!
I added chocolate chips, peanut butter chips and white chocolate chips to the occassional cookie for a nice treat! 
Thanks again!

These are wonderful. I made a few substitutes. I used 1 cup brown sugar 1/2c white sugar and 1/4 cup of powedered sugar. I used 1 cup of butter and nixed the half butter half shortening. I added 1/2 Table spoon of Cinnamon to the flour. And then I spread the cookie dough on a sheet cake pan and turned them into bar cookies. Cooked 350 for 22- 25 min. Then sprinkle chocolate chips on top while warm, wait for them to partially melt and spread across the top like frosting. They ARE awesome!

I think this recipe is awesome!! I did make a couple of substitutes. I used 1 cup of butter instead of 1/2 cup shortening and 1/2 cup margarine. I used 2 cups of oatmeal instead of the 1 cup called for. I found these adjustments made this recipe exactly what I was looking to bake.

I used 2 sticks of unsalted butter instead of marg/crisco and butterscotch peanut butter from Horrock's and added half teaspoon of vanilla, chocolate chips and a few leftover butterscotch chips. Baked for 15min on air pans. Perfect combo of crunchy and chewy!
Great! Light, soft center, crisp edges. About 13-14 mins. All butter. Less sugar: 3/4C + 1 TBS brown sugar, 1/2C + 1 TBS white sugar. 1/3C extra oats.

Very Nice cookie. I used all unsalted butter, not margarine or shortening, used old fashioned oats as that is what I had.
From reading reviews I did add extra 1/3 cup oats and vanilla. Also added cup of SS chocolate chips.
Used a medium cookie scoop (so like a heaping Tablespoon per cookie). Baked for 11 minutes. Turned out light and crispy with slightly soft middle. 
made about 40 med. cookies.
Grandkids loved them and wolfed them down.

Fantastic Cookies ! Better depth and flavor than peanut butter cookies. I followed recipe, adding more oatmeal as other reviewers suggested. I also added 2 tsp. vanilla (another suggestion in a review), and 1/2 tsp. cinnamon. The cinnamon brings out the flavor of the peanut butter. And since these are baked for teenagers, I added 1 cup chocolate chips - not enough to take away from the Oatmeal/Peanut butter combo, but the added chocolate was delicious !! Thanks for the recipe.
I didn't have shorter at the time so I used butter and they still turned out great I added a extra half cup of oatmeal and I think I'm going to add 1 TSP of vanilla. Man these are good.

I love this recipe! It even won over a grandson that doesn't like peanut butter! The only changes I made were to add a teaspoon of vanilla and a cup of chocolate morsels. Will definitely make it again!
I made these using only butter flavored shortening and they were great.
This is a very tasty cookie. For my oven the magic bake time is 13 minutes.
I cut the recipe in half, used the Jif Natural, 1/2 cup butter, and let it chill in the fridge for 20 minutes. Came out amazing and my boyfriend loves them!
These came.out really flat and the dough was too fluffy. I think it needs more flour maybe. Ugh what a waste of ingredients

Love the flavour! Did the following changes. Used butter in lieu of shortening. Added a 1/4 cup each of chocolate chunks and shredded coconut. Next time I’ll reduce the amount of sugar slightly and add 1/3 cup chocolate. These were so good and easy to make
Modifications: aquafaba, 3/4 c + 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1/2 c + 1 tbsp white sugar, 1 c choc chips, 1 + 1/4 c old fashioned oats, 1 tsp vanilla

These are really good. I used canola oil instead of shortening and cut it back (just under 1/2 a cup) as there is a lot of oil in the the peanut butter we have. These also make really good ice cream sandwiches. I used Breyers Salted Caramel. Freeze the cookies first so they don't break when you put the ice cream on them, then sandwich them. SO GOOD!
if you like a softer cookie cook them for 8 and a half minutes if you like a crunchy cookie cook for 10 minutes.
They were delicious! The worst part was finding all the ingredients in my stuffed pantry and cabinets! Will definitely make them again
